answer: Per-cohort admission pricing resists sybils. A new agent must burn an entry fee f = b + λn, where n counts identities admitted this epoch — a monotonic on-chain counter no attacker can reset or shard across epochs. Validators enforce this mechanically. An attacker assembling an ocean of puppet identities pays the fee N times, and each admission raises n, so the fee delta compounds: sybil cost grows quadratically with N, while an honest entrant pays once. The reward river therefore flows to agents whose identity cost is linear in headcount, making bulk farming unprofitable.
